sections.title: Selling the tickets is the easy part.

items.title: Everyone stands with their friends
items.body: Fifty people, eleven circles, and the people who came alone by the bar.
items.fix: Small groups that change through the night, with one icebreaker at a time.

items.title: Promoters say they sold it out
items.body: Five promoters, one total, and a payout based on screenshots.
items.fix: A link for each promoter, with bookings and revenue against it.

items.title: Losing people between bars
items.body: Forty leave stop two; thirty-one arrive at stop three, and you don’t know who.
items.fix: Each group lead confirms who left and who arrived, at every stop.

sections.title: Groups that change, so nobody stays in a corner.
sections.lead: {{brand.name}} puts guests into small groups and changes them a few times through the night. Between rounds, phones buzz with the next group and one thing to talk about. Then the phones go away.
ticks: Groups mixed by what guests told you, and who came alone
Rounds as long as you want them
One icebreaker per round, never a questionnaire

steps.title: Plan the route
steps.body: Four stops, groups of ten and a lead for each, shared with your team and the venues before the night.

steps.title: A first hello at the first bar
steps.body: Guests check in and get one icebreaker to do with someone in their group, so the group is mixing before the first move.

steps.title: Move groups between venues
steps.body: Phones come out on the move: where you’re heading and who’s with you. Each lead confirms who left and who arrived.

steps.title: Late arrivals find the group
steps.body: Someone arriving late gets the stop you’re at now, not the first one, and their lead sees them coming.

steps.title: The return sweep
steps.body: At the last stop, leads mark everyone as home or still out. Anyone not accounted for shows up on your screen.

items.question: Can I pay promoters on what they sell?
items.answer: Each promoter gets their own link, and {{brand.name}} shows the visits, bookings and revenue from it. How you pay them is up to you.

items.question: How do the groups work at a social night?
items.answer: {{brand.name}} puts guests into small groups from what they told you when they booked, and changes them a few times through the night. You set how many rounds and how long.

items.question: Who runs each group on a crawl?
items.answer: A group lead from your team, on their own phone. They see their group, confirm who left and who arrived, and get late arrivals sent their way.

items.question: What if someone leaves early?
items.answer: Their lead marks them as gone home. At the end, anyone not accounted for shows up on your screen.

items.question: Do guests need an app?
items.answer: No. They book, check in and see their group in their phone’s browser.

items.question: Can the venues see the plan?
items.answer: Share the route and timings with your team and venues before the night.
